findings.title: getCredentials NPE for users not in federated map
findings.body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java at line 232, getCredentials() does var myUser = getMyUser(user) then dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes without a null check, while isConfiguredFor() and isValid() explicitly handle null. When the storage provider is enabled Keycloak calls getFederatedCredentialsStream/getCredentials for every user including purely local users not in the users map, so myUser is null and this throws NullPointerException, breaking credential listing and login for unrelated users.

findings.title: Federated recovery-code validation does not consume codes
findings.body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java at line 340, isValid() for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only does generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...) and returns true without removing or marking the used code as consumed. The local keycloak-recovery-authn-codes provider makes codes single-use and tracks allCodesUsed() to force regeneration and deletion. With this implementation the same federated recovery code can be replayed indefinitely, allCodesUsed() never becomes true, and the test only logs in once so reuse is never caught.

findings.title: Federated getCredentials discards stored credential ID
findings.body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java at line 237, getCredentials() builds the returned value via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) which creates a new CredentialModel with a fresh ID, discarding the ID assigned in updateCredential() to myUser.recoveryCodes. Any later operation by ID such as account-console DELETE /credentials/{id} or RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.removeStoredCredentialById() when all codes are used will use an ID that does not match the stored federated credential, so deletion silently fails and a stale credential remains.

findings.title: Federated recovery codes cannot be disabled/deleted
findings.body: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java at line 217, disableCredentialType() only handles OTP types and logs unsupported for anything else, and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() at line 254 only advertises OTP. As a result admin disableCredentialType and account-management deletion for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE are no-ops for federated users: federated recovery codes can never be removed via the supported APIs and remain valid.

findings.title: Unchecked Optional.get() causes 500 on recovery login
findings.body: In RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java at line 19, the constructor calls RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) then immediately does credentialModelOpt.get() without checking isPresent. A user-storage provider is allowed to implement CredentialInputValidator.isValid without exposing credentials via getCredentials(), or the credential may be missing/mismatched between federated and local stores. In that case this throws NoSuchElementException and produces a 500 error when rendering the recovery-code login form instead of a handled authentication failure.

findings.title: Raw recovery codes sent to user storage in plaintext
findings.body: In CredentialHelper.java at line 123, createRecoveryCodesCredential() serializes the raw generatedCodes list to JSON and passes it as the UserCredentialModel to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(), while the local path stores only hashed codes inside RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel. External user storage therefore persists recoverable plaintext recovery codes, as demonstrated by the test provider storing credentialData verbatim, so compromise of the external store yields all codes. Hashed material could be stored and verified like the local provider does.

findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery credential never removed
findings.body: In RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java at line 86, after successful validation the code loads the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() which now may return a federated credential and then calls removeStoredCredentialById() when allCodesUsed(). Federated credentials are managed via the UserStorageProvider disable path, which the bundled test provider does not implement for recovery codes, so for federated users this deletion is a no-op: exhausted codes remain stored and the addRequiredAction(CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES) logic dependent on removal breaks.
